observed_evidence.summary: Reuters reported that VLCC freight from the Gulf of Oman to China reached about Worldscale 450, equivalent to roughly US$11.50 per barrel, the highest since the rate was introduced earlier in 2026. The rise followed the largest wave of shipping attacks since the U.S.-Iran war began and coincided with Houthi advances near Bab el-Mandeb.

Persistent tanker-rate inflation would raise delivered energy costs in Asia even if spot crude prices ease, increasing imported inflation and margin pressure for Taiwan energy users while improving pricing power for selected shipping operators.
